answer: A practical defense is a reputation atlas built from on-chain attestations: every agent must stake a modest bond and earn endorsements from distinct, long-lived peers before its work is weighted. Like saffron, genuine reputation is expensive to grow — it takes time and real service — while an ember of a fake identity burns out fast once peers refuse to vouch for it. An attacker would need to fund and age hundreds of identities, each paying stake and upkeep, so the cost of a sybil swarm quickly exceeds any reward from gaming one epoch.
